module purpose: This module decodes selected control-bus instruction fields and operand inputs into enabled crypto coprocessor operations, latches the accepted operands and function bits, computes xperm, SHA, SM3, AES, and SM4 word transforms, and returns a 32-bit result on res_o with a completion indication on valid_o. A small FSM adds a busy/done sequence for the multi-cycle classes and reset clears the stored context and control state.

use-case flows.value: recognize a supported crypto instruction, qualify it for this coprocessor, and capture its operand and function fields
xperm word result from rs1 and rs2 when EN_ZBKX is enabled
SHA helper word result from rs1 and rs2 under funct12 selection when EN_ZKNH is enabled
SM3 helper word result from rs1 under funct12 selection when EN_ZKSH is enabled
AES or SM4 block-cipher word transform using a selected rs2 byte, optional S-box and mix/round logic, byte rotation, and xor with rs1
selected result word on res_o and completion indication on valid_o
clear stored operand/context registers, control state, result register, and resettable block-cipher pipeline registers while rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.concept: Latched operand words of the accepted crypto instruction
conceptual assets.reasoning: The start flow copies rs1_i and rs2_i into rs1 and rs2 only when cmd_valid = '1' (lines 312-314). Those stored operands are then consumed by xperm (lines 383, 389), SHA (lines 413-425), SM3 (line 441), and the block-cipher xor/result path (lines 456-475). Integrity is established because corrupting either stored operand changes the implemented result formulas; availability is also established because multi-cycle commands pass through S_BUSY/S_DONE (lines 324-337) and still depend on the preserved operands when res_o is written (lines 354-367).

Control fields from ctrl_i are decoded into cmd (lines 274-293), qualified into cmd_valid (line 296), and latched as funct3 and funct12 on acceptance (lines 315-316). These stored selectors choose the xperm variant (line 393), SHA variant (lines 411-425), SM3 variant (line 441), block-cipher byte select and rotation (lines 456-468), AES encrypt/decrypt mode (line 494), and the result source via out_sel (lines 355-365, 372). The FSM state and done registers sequence S_IDLE/S_BUSY/S_DONE and generate the completion indication exported on valid_o (lines 320-343). Integrity is established because wrong control or selector state executes the wrong transform, picks the wrong result source, or signals completion at the wrong time; availability is established because accepted requests advance through the implemented state transitions and completion pulse generation of lines 323-337 and 343.

When EN_ZBKX is enabled, xperm8_res and xperm4_res are formed from rs1 and selected byte or nibble fields of rs2 (lines 381-390), and xperm_res selects between them with funct3(2) (line 393). The report flow writes res_o <= xperm_res when out_sel = "100" and done = '1' (line 357). Integrity is established because the consumer depends on receiving exactly that selected permutation result; availability is established in builds with EN_ZBKX, while the disabled build ties the xperm path to zero (lines 397-401).

When EN_ZKNH is enabled, sha_res is computed from rs1 alone or from rs1 together with rs2 according to funct12 (lines 409-425). In the result process, the non-xperm/non-block path writes res_o <= sha_res when the SM3-specific condition is false (lines 360-365, especially line 364). Integrity is established because the reported word must match the selected shift/rotate formula; availability is established in builds with EN_ZKNH, while the disabled build forces sha_res to zero (lines 431-433).

When EN_ZKSH is enabled, sm3_res is computed from rs1 with one of two rotate-xor formulas selected by funct12(0) (line 441). The result process writes res_o <= sm3_res when EN_ZKSH and ctrl_i.ir_opcode(5) = '0' and funct12(3) = '1' (lines 361-362). Integrity is established because the exported word must match that selected formula; availability is established in builds with EN_ZKSH, while the disabled build forces sm3_res to zero (lines 444-446).

conceptual assets.concept: Block-cipher result word for the AES/SM4 instruction path
conceptual assets.reasoning: When any of EN_ZKNE, EN_ZKND, or EN_ZKSED is enabled, rs2_sel selects one byte of rs2 (lines 456-460). The AES path stores an S-box lookup in aes.so (line 500), transforms it into aes.mix1 with decrypt- or encrypt-specific coefficients (lines 510-519), and forms aes.mix2 (line 525). The SM4 path stores an S-box lookup in sm4.so1 (line 547) and a transformed round word in sm4.rnd (lines 560-565). Common logic rotates the selected word and forms blk_res <= rs1 xor rol_res (lines 463-475), and the report flow writes res_o <= blk_res when out_sel is 101 or 110 and done = '1' (lines 358-359). Integrity is established because the consumer depends on the exact AES/SM4 data-path word defined by those lines; availability is established only in builds where the relevant path is enabled, while the disabled alternatives tie the path to zero (lines 479-484, 529-534, 572-576).
